claims.paraphrase: Page title.
createRenderer sanitizes by default with a floor.
One switch turns the sanitize floor off.
Section heading.
Editors author through a web form, unlike a trusted-content static-site generator.
The realistic threat is a compromised editor account or pasted script, not an anonymous attacker.
Editors are a small owner-curated allowlist.
Editors commit through the site GitHub App.
Without a floor any editor could run script in every visitor browser.
Section heading.
Stage order inside createRenderer is fixed and mixes remark and rehype steps.
Diagram of the nine ordered stages and the two the switch turns off.
The switch disables only the floor and the sink guard; stages between them keep running.
Pointer to the rendering configuration page.
sanitizeSchema extends the allowlist the floor uses.
remarkPlugins and rehypePlugins compose at the last stage of the diagram.
Section heading.
Every renderer runs a rehype-sanitize floor from the GitHub-lineage default schema unless a site opts out.
A site does not wire the floor up.
The floor exists because the reference delivery path once had none.
Section heading.
sanitizeSchema receives the default schema and returns the schema to use, additively.
There is no supported way to remove a strip entry or re-admit script through this option.
unsafeDisableSanitize is a code-level switch removing both the floor and the guard, not an editor setting.
Do not reach for the switch because a sanitize finding is inconvenient.
Section heading.
On top of the default schema the built one adds a short specific list.
The directive markers survive the floor as inert data attributes for the dispatch step.
Five extra tags (nav, details, summary, figure, figcaption) are allowlisted.
className is admitted on any element after dropping the default anchor exception.
srcSet and sizes are admitted on img.
The inert cairn: scheme is admitted on href while javascript: and data: stay stripped.
Section heading.
The floor runs ahead of build() so trusted output and inline SVG icons are never sanitized.
A build() function is site code that can route a raw attribute into a sink built after the floor.
rehypeSinkGuard runs after anchor hardening and strips on* and style and scheme-checks URL properties.
The sink guard runs under the same switch as the floor.
The guard leaves a build-emitted script, style, or iframe srcdoc element in place.
A component author reaching for those elements is running their own code.
Section heading.
Raw HTML is parsed by rehype-raw and cleaned to the allowlist, never delivered verbatim or dropped.
Section heading.
Every target blank anchor gets its rel forced after highlighting and ahead of the sink guard.
Anchors that components build get the same hardening as anchors authors type.
Syntax highlighting emits class-only output and needs no special placement.
Section heading.
A registered component can bypass these guarantees by rendering trusted markup outside the sanitized tree.
